chunks: Imran al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

about a man who performed tawaf of the House and the sa'i between Safa and Marwa while having performed tamattu', then hastened and kissed his wife before trimming his hair. He (the Imam) said: 'Upon him is a dam (sheep) which he must slaughter, and if he had intercourse, then upon him is a juzur (camel) or a cow.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Safa and Marwa (the two hills between which sa'i is performed)
key_terms.بَقَرَةٌ: Baqarah (a cow, an alternative higher-value sacrifice)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Dam (a specific sacrificial animal, typically a sheep, offered as expiation)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who kisses or has intercourse with his wife before trimming his hair after Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that a mutamatti' pilgrim who prematurely engages in intimacy before the final haircut must offer a sheep (dam) for kissing or a camel/cow for full intercourse, reflecting the graduated severity of the breach. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of the mutamatti' compared to the mufrid, where the Hajj and Umrah are performed separately, and emphasizes the importance of maintaining the state of Ihram integrity until the ritual haircut is completed. The differentiation in expiation underscores the scholarly view that the prohibition applies specifically to the period between the completion of Umrah rites and the final release from Ihram.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2743 - Imran al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who performed tawaf of the Kaaba and the sa'i between Safa and Marwa while performing tamattu‘, then hastened and kissed his wife before trimming his hair.
Imam (as) said: "He must offer a sacrifice of a sheep. If he engaged in intercourse, he must offer a camel or a cow."
